title: Agent frameworks and MCP
description: Use DID.is from MCP clients, LangChain and the OpenAI Agents SDK, either as a remote MCP server or as a guard in front of your own tools.
---

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

There are two ways to use DID.is with an agent. They solve different problems and can be combined.

- **Let the agent look things up** (resolve a DID, verify a credential, inspect an MCP server or A2A card): connect the DID.is MCP server at `https://did.is/mcp`. No account and no API key.
- **Stop a tool from running** unless the tool is unchanged and the agent was delegated to call it: put the SDK guard (`@didis/client` or `didis-py`) in your own code. See [Guard agent tools](/build/guard-tools/).

## The DID.is MCP server

`https://did.is/mcp` is a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP). All of its tools are read-only and return the same results as the [public API](/build/api-overview/).

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `resolve_did` | Resolve a DID and report which evidence is established. |
| `verify_credential` | Verify a W3C Verifiable Credential or SD-JWT VC. |
| `inspect_mcp_server` | Inspect another MCP server: protocol version, tool fingerprints, annotations. |
| `inspect_a2a_agent` | Fetch an A2A agent card and report its signature status. |
| `authorize_tool_call` | Check whether a delegation chain allows an agent to call a tool. |
| `evaluate_policy` | Evaluate a DID against declarative rules. |
| `search_directory` | Search the public directory of DIDs whose controllers proved control. |

Fields under `untrusted` in a result are third-party content. The agent should not follow instructions found there. `INDETERMINATE` is never a pass. If a result says to wait, the agent should wait that many seconds before the next call.

### Connect an MCP client

No sign-in is needed. After connecting, ask the agent to use a DID.is tool, for example "Resolve did:web:did.is with DID.is", and check that the tool call appears in the session.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="Claude Code">
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http didis https://did.is/mcp
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="VS Code">
Run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, enter `https://did.is/mcp` and use `didis` as the server ID.
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Cursor">
`mcp.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "didis": { "url": "https://did.is/mcp" }
  }
}
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Use it from agent code

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="Python">
OpenAI Agents SDK:
```python
import asyncio
from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStreamableHttp

async def main() -> None:
    async with MCPServerStreamableHttp(params={"url": "https://did.is/mcp"}) as didis:
        agent = Agent(name="Checker", instructions="Use DID.is to check identifiers.", mcp_servers=[didis])
        result = await Runner.run(agent, "Resolve did:web:did.is and say what is established.")
        print(result.final_output)

asyncio.run(main())
```

LangChain (`langchain-mcp-adapters`):
```python
import asyncio
from langchain_mcp_adapters.client import MultiServerMCPClient

async def main() -> None:
    client = MultiServerMCPClient({"didis": {"transport": "streamable_http", "url": "https://did.is/mcp"}})
    tools = await client.get_tools()   # pass these tools to your agent
    print([t.name for t in tools])

asyncio.run(main())
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
MCP TypeScript SDK:
```ts
import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js";
import { StreamableHTTPClientTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/streamableHttp.js";

const client = new Client({ name: "my-agent", version: "1.0.0" });
await client.connect(new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL("https://did.is/mcp")));

const result = await client.callTool({ name: "resolve_did", arguments: { did: "did:web:did.is" } });
console.log(result.content);
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Guard your own tools

The MCP server answers questions. It does not stop anything. To make sure a tool runs only when it is unchanged and delegated, put the SDK guard in front of the tool. Complete examples, runnable without an account or an LLM key:

| Framework | TypeScript | Python |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP client (official SDKs) | [`mcp-client.mjs`](https://github.com/did-is/didis-js/blob/main/examples/mcp-client.mjs) | [`mcp_client.py`](https://github.com/did-is/didis-py/blob/main/examples/mcp_client.py) |
| LangChain | [`langchain-tool.mjs`](https://github.com/did-is/didis-js/blob/main/examples/langchain-tool.mjs) | [`langchain_tool.py`](https://github.com/did-is/didis-py/blob/main/examples/langchain_tool.py) |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | [`openai-agents-tool.mjs`](https://github.com/did-is/didis-js/blob/main/examples/openai-agents-tool.mjs) | [`openai_agents_tool.py`](https://github.com/did-is/didis-py/blob/main/examples/openai_agents_tool.py) |

[Guard agent tools](/build/guard-tools/#use-with-mcp-and-agent-frameworks) explains where the check goes in each framework.
